record_type_quote:
Push button reproduction attempt of a research claim from Ernst Fehr, Oliver Hart and
Christian Zehnder, (2011), in American Economic Review

targets.authors: Fehr, Ernst, Oliver Hart, and Christian Zehnder
targets.title: Contracts as Reference Points—Experimental Evidence
targets.evidence_quote: Claim paragraph: We selected the claim that there is considerable seller shading in flexible contracts in the good state. In contrast, there is almost no shading in rigid contracts. This reflects the following statement from the paper’s abstract: “Flexible contracts—-which would dominate rigid contracts under standard assumptions—-cause significant shading in ex post performance, while under rigid contracts much less shading occurs.” The claim was tested by a nonparametric signed rank test between rigid and flexible contracts on price paid, which resulted in the difference in the frequency of shading between the two contract types being statistically significant (nonparametric signed rank test, p-value = 0.031 (one-sided)).
targets.outcome_computational_quote: Reproduction result: Analyst was able to reproduce the results after the extended PBR attempt – The difference in the frequency of shading between the two contract types being statistically significant (nonparametric signed rank test, p-value = 0.031 (one-sided)).
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: The one-sided p-value of the above test is 0.0313. The analyst also tried this process for two other results in the paper, section III.A.2, paragraph 1 and section III.A.1, paragraph 1 and the results match the ones reported in the manuscript.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The extended attempt recovered the focal numbers after reconstructing missing commands. The report only reproduces reported tests; it does not test alternative specifications.
